set.relation: Umbrella for current-state, initial-state, initial-final, K-step, infinite-step and pre-opacity; its infinite-step form is the paper's dual of diagnosability ('always not know' vs. 'always eventually know'); related to noninterference; several classes expressed as hyperproperties (HyperLTL).

More challenging alternative to the secret-revelation-probability formulation; often undecidable (linked to probabilistic-automaton emptiness), hence belief-state abstractions and sufficient conditions.

set.gloss: A system is diagnosable if, once a fault occurs, its occurrence can be inferred with certainty from the observations within a finite delay.
set.relation: Dual of infinite-step opacity; related to detectability, observability and prognosability. The paper does not mention monitorability: the analogy (a monitor inferring misbehavior from partial observations) is the map's.

adds.quote: We assume that Vrec and Vsen have matched public capability: they differ only in their access to the shared key k. Formally, let A be any random variable that does not depend on S or k.
adds.formula: \forall A\ \text{not depending on}\ S\ \text{or}\ k:\quad U^{u}_{\mathcal V_{\mathrm{rec}}}(Y\mid X^{\mathrm{aud}},Z_0,A)=U^{u}_{\mathcal V_{\mathrm{sen}}}(Y\mid X^{\mathrm{aud}},Z_0,A)
adds.assumptions: Composite signal Z = (Z0, Enc(S, k)) with public component Z0 and a payload S under a shared key k; Receiver and Sentinel decoder families; an auditing task (Y, u) and context X^aud.
adds.where: Assumption E.3, App. E.2, Eq. (30), [P551]-[P553]; Proposition E.10, [P590]
adds.gloss: Receiver and Sentinel decoders do equally well on everything except the shared key, so any gap must come from the keyed payload; without this, a weaker Sentinel yields a positive gap with no encoding.
adds.relation: Premise of Theorems E.6-E.7 and Corollary E.8; Proposition E.10 shows that violating it gives false positives. Formal version of the main text's trusted Sentinel 'with comparable capabilities'.
